land.text: Bulungan, the eastern shores of North Kalimantan toward Tawau, 'completely incorporated ... into the Dutch East Indies in June 1878'

successors.note: The sultanate kept a Dutch-supervised ruler: self-administration (zelfbestuur) in 1928, accession to Indonesia on 17 August 1949, abolition as a regency in 1959 (page). This dossier ends at the 1878 incorporation.

capitals.name: Salim Batu
capitals.note: 'Wira Amir moved his capital from Busang Arau to Salim Batu' (1731; the capital table has Limbu 1695-1731 before). Coordinates approximate (the page gives none).

capitals.name: Tanjung Palas
capitals.note: 'Aji Ali ... moved the capital from Salim Batu to Tanjung Palas' (1777); the table has Tanjung Palas to 1928, Tarakan 1928-1933. Coordinates approximate. The Dutch set up a government post at Tanjung Selor in 1893.

rulers.name: Datuk Alam (Sultan Khalifatul Alam Muhammad Adil)
Ali Kahar (Sultan Kaharuddin II)
rulers.note: Reigned beyond the dossier's end (1878) under Dutch incorporation.

ledger.note: 1731: Wira Amir, newly Muslim as Sultan Amiril Mukminin, founds the sultanate. 'In 1731, this dynasty, now under Wira Amir, who recently converted to Islam as Sultan Amiril Mukminin. ... This marked the foundation of Bulungan as a sultanate.' The page also has 'Bulungan ... a vassal of the sultan of Berau', so the new sultanate stood under Berau until 1789.

ledger.note: 1731: the new sultanate stands under Berau. Infobox: 'Vassal of the Sultanate of Berau (1731-1789)'; text: 'Bulungan was recognised as a vassal of the sultan of Berau, the latter acknowledging himself a vassal of Kutai.' Berau has no dossier (counterpart written as the page's name; the Berau pages did not load in the first run).
1731: the capital moves from Busang Arau to Salim Batu ('Wira Amir moved his capital from Busang Arau to Salim Batu'; the capital table has Limbu 1695-1731).
1777: Sultan Alimuddin moves the capital to Tanjung Palas ('Aji Ali succeeded his father as Sultan Alimuddin and moved the capital from Salim Batu to Tanjung Palas').

Infobox: 'Vassal of the Sultanate of Sulu (1789-1855)'; text: 'After the civil war in Berau, Sulu sacked both Berau and Tarakan in 1789' and 'By the early 19th century, Sulu became the dominant power in northeastern Borneo'. Mirrors sultanate-of-sulu /ledger/5.

ledger.note: 1789: Bulungan 'declared independence from Berau' after Sulu sacked Berau (page; infobox ends the vassalage in 1789).

27 September 1834: Bulungan becomes a Dutch protectorate. After the Dutch conquered Berau in 1834 they 'forced the sultan to sign an agreement on 27 September', 'making Bulungan an official Dutch protectorate'. Infobox: 'Protectorate of the Dutch East Indies (1834-1878)'. The infobox overlaps this with Sulu's overlordship to 1855.

the Tidung Lands and the Sebuku River villages toward Tawau; 'the jurisdiction of Bulungan extended all the way towards Tawau'

ledger.note: 1849: the Tidungs are subjugated. 'In 1849, he went to war with the Tidungs and subjugated them under his rule. During this period, the jurisdiction of Bulungan extended all the way towards Tawau.' In February 1849 the residents of three Sebuku River villages had pledged to Sulu and Bulungan used force against them (page). The Tawau disc is the researcher's reading of 'towards Tawau'; the Tidung states have no dossier.

ledger.note: 1855: 'Bulungan stopped paying tribute to Sulu for 50 years, thereby becoming de facto independent from Sulu' (infobox: Sulu vassalage 1789-1855; the page adds that the influence 'officially ended in 1878'). Mirrors sultanate-of-sulu /ledger/6.

ledger.note: June 1878: the protectorate (infobox 1834-1878) ends in annexation; 'Bulungan was finally incorporated into the colonial empire of the Dutch East Indies in June 1878'. The dissolve below carries the incorporation.

June 1878: the Dutch incorporate Bulungan. 'the Dutch completely incorporated Bulungan into the Dutch East Indies in June 1878' (infobox: 'Annexation into the Dutch East Indies: 1878'). Sultans continue under Dutch supervision to 1959.

certainty.note: Forest and river frontiers with the Tidung Lands, Berau and the Apo Kayan interior; the 1913/1915 British-Dutch border agreements come after this dossier ends.

notes:
Page budget 1-2: one page opened; the second (Berau, then Sultanate of Berau) did not load (URL_NOT_FOUND twice: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berau_Sultanate and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultanate_of_Berau). (1) Cliopatria's row stops in 1747 but the page's sultanate runs to 1878 (incorporation) and 1959 (regency); the dossier adds new keyframes 1731-1733, 1748-1848 and 1849-1878 from the same outline. (2) The dossier ends at the 1878 incorporation; the three vassalages of the infobox are now in this ledger (see REVISION below); the infobox overlaps the Sulu and Dutch statuses 1834-1855, so which tint shows in those years is the renderer's call. (3) Berau (suzerain 1731-1789, 'in turn a vassal of Kutai') has no dossier before Sambaliung (1830); the counterpart is the string 'Berau Sultanate' and sultanate-of-berau is listed as needing a dossier. (4) The Tawau cut and the 1849 gain are readings of one undated sentence. (5) Capital coordinates are approximate. (6) Pre-1731 history on the page (Datuk Mencang 1555-1595 at Busang Arau; Limbu 1695-1731) has no territory and is left out. (7) The Cliopatria outline is 20,247 km2 against no page figure. Gazetteer names needed: Bulungan (region), Tanjung Palas, Salim Batu, Tanjung Selor, Tidung Lands, Sebuku (river).

REVISION 2026-10-19 (after review): page re-opened (Sultanate of Bulungan). Added the vassal pairs with counterpart = the suzerain, because rule 4 puts both sides of a vassalage in the vassal's ledger: Berau Sultanate 1731-1789 (infobox 'Vassal of the Sultanate of Berau (1731-1789)'; 'declared independence from Berau'), sultanate-of-sulu 1789-1855 (infobox 'Vassal of the Sultanate of Sulu (1789-1855)'; 'stopped paying tribute to Sulu'), dutch-east-indies 27 September 1834 to June 1878 (infobox 'Protectorate of the Dutch East Indies (1834-1878)'). The 1834 event, formerly a rename caption, is now vassal_start. The three statuses overlap in 1789-1855 exactly as the infobox lists them; I did not choose between them. Disagreement with the reviewer's thin points: none. Still open: the extent before 1849 (the Tawau cut) rests on the one undated sentence 'During this period, the jurisdiction of Bulungan extended all the way towards Tawau'; the page names no Tidung lands or Berau frontier, and I did not open Berau Regency or Tarakan (page budget 1-2, one page re-opened). The Tidung states (counterpart of the 1849 gain) still need a dossier. The page has no area figure (checked again).
